How to read this. Each section is a menu tab of the app, in sidebar order. Inside it, one diagram per screen or task, from the first click to where the flow ends or hands off.

The shape tells you the kind of step and the colour tells you who does it (see the sixteen shapes below). Dashed boxes that say Continues in are links: click one to jump to that diagram. Type any button label or screen name in the search box to find every diagram that uses it. Drag a diagram to move it; use Full screen for the big ones.

No diagram mentions that. Try a button label, a screen name or an agent name.

Overview

How to read the diagrams, the whole site map, and one request from referral to decision.

The sixteen shapes

The shape says what kind of step it is. The colour says who does it. Every diagram in this document uses only these.

Start

Where the flow begins: a sidebar click, a link, an event

End (done)

The flow finishes normally

End (stopped)

The flow stops: blocked, declined, cancelled, nothing to do

Screen

A page the person sees

Pop-up

A drawer, modal, menu or panel on top of a screen

Person clicks

A person's click, tap, key press or signature

Person enters

A person types, picks, drops or uploads something

System step

What the app does: validate, calculate, update the screen

FLO / agent

Automated work by FLO or one of the agents (Reader, Scribe, ...)

Decision

A yes/no or multi-way branch; every exit is labelled

Data saved

A record is created or changed (case, request, referral, mapping, rule)

Document

A letter, brief, report, appeal, form or file produced or read

Outside party

Payer, referrer, EMR or portal: something outside Psyflo acts

Wait

Time passes or the flow waits on someone

Message

A toast, banner or notification the person sees

Continues elsewhere

Jumps to another diagram; the label names it

Blue: a personPurple: FLO and the agentsGrey: the appOrange: outside partyAmber: decisionTeal: data savedCream: screenGreen and red: the ends

How to read these diagrams

One example flow that uses every shape once. The shape tells you what kind of step it is; the colour tells you who does it.

Global shell › Top bar › Ask FLO › What FLO answers

      
FLO lowercases the question and tries six rules in order. The first rule that matches answers, so a question with two key words gets the earlier answer. Counts, names and the request or denial it points to come from the live demo data. Only the Cardinal answer is fixed text.

      
Typed questions use the same rules as the suggestion chips. FLO does not look at which page is open. Every link opens a view that matches the answer. PRD 08 describes row-level citations, thumbs and an escalate action on each answer; the demo gives one paragraph and one link instead.

Dashboard › Request drawer › Answer a payer information request

      
When a payer asks for more information, Packet drafts the answer from the chart, Integrity checks it, and a person reads it and signs. Nothing leaves before the signature. In the demo the payer's ask is seeded or triggered by a Demo control, and the send is simulated.

      
Real world: an information request is tracked, and a clinical supplement passes the clinician sign-off gate before it goes out. Demo only: one click on 'Sign and send answer' stands in for that, and the send is simulated.

Dashboard › Request drawer › Demo controls: the payer answers

      
A dashed 'Demo controls' box at the end of every drawer lets the presenter pretend the payer replied. Nothing is sent anywhere. A request only moves forward, so the box offers only the replies still ahead of it. This diagram covers when buttons show and the replies that keep a request alive; approve, approve part and deny are in the next diagram.

      
Demo only: in real life the payer answers through its portal, fax or phone and Navigator finds out by checking. These buttons fake that answer; nothing is sent.

Dashboard › Request drawer › Demo controls: approve, approve part or deny

      
The three final payer answers and what the Dashboard shows afterwards. They are offered on a Received, Under review or Info requested request, and after one of them no more replies are offered. An approval stays on the Dashboard with a write-back waiting. A partial approval or a denial turns the request into a new D- number and hands it to Denial Intelligence.

      
Demo only: the payer's decision is simulated. Real rules: a decision is due in 7 days (72 hours when expedited), and a partial approval or denial goes to the denial route, starting with a peer-to-peer call.

Payers › Process › Save the workflow

      
'Save workflow' asks for a reason, then makes the edited steps the payer's next version. New drafts use the new version at once; sent requests keep what they were sent with; open drafts wait for 'Update drafts'. Escape closes one pop-up at a time, so it never throws away the editor's edits by accident. There is no undo: a change is reversed by editing again, and the edit log keeps the old text.

Settings

  
The sixteen agents, how much freedom each has, Pause all.

  
  


  

    

      
Settings › Agents › Arrive and read the sixteen agents

      
The Settings page is one screen about the agents: who they are, how much freedom each one has, a switch for each, and a button to pause them all. This shows what the person sees and what each row says.

      
Every level and switch is kept in the app, not in the page. Leave Settings and come back and nothing has changed. 'Reset demo data' puts every agent back to its starting level with its switch on.

Settings › Agents › Change an agent's freedom

      
Each of the sixteen rows has a Freedom dropdown with three levels. Picking one saves it for that agent and shows a toast. EMR Connect reads it: 'Ask before acting' makes Sync now, Fix and Reconnect ask first, and 'Act on its own' logs without a toast.

      
The level is kept in the app, so it is still there after leaving Settings. Only 'Reset demo data' puts the starting levels back. The 'What each level changes' card on the page says where a level applies.

Settings › Agents › What each freedom level allows and the gates it never skips

      
The three levels set how much an agent does before a person looks. Five gates sit above every level. The page names the levels, says in one line what each changes (the 'What each level changes' card) and shows the Gates card. The PRD guardrail matrix gives the wider meaning.

      
The mapping from the three demo labels to the PRD words (Stage or Draft, Auto + notify, Auto) is our reading. The PRD sets autonomy per action, not per agent. In the demo the levels are applied in EMR Connect only.
